canonical_definition: Natural Language Understanding (NLU) refers to the ability to comprehend and process natural language across a range of tasks, often operationalized through evaluation on the GLUE benchmark. While some definitions emphasize general language competence that persists after model fine-tuning or adaptation, others specify narrower requirements for tasks like linguistic acceptability, sentiment analysis, paraphrase detection, or semantic inference. Disagreements exist in scope: certain papers frame NLU as a broad capability for language comprehension (including code intent analysis or caption generation), while others tie it more strictly to standardized NLP benchmarks.
